description: Shared parity cases for the colour-slot linear program of NU-053. The inputs (places, coloured places, marking, flat rows with pre and post counts) are written by hand. Each 'expected' object is written by the Rust script-parity test under scripts/smt-script-parity.py --update and read by every implementation: status, presolved places and rows, pivots, work (entry updates), optimum, k and the scaled weighting (non-zero weights by place, and the denominator).

cases.note: A reset arc on the uncoloured budget keeps a free weight there (no H1): optimum 4.
An all(budget) drain beside the loop: optimum 4.
Arrivals(3) closed into a source; the decline row destroys a token, so no semiflow covers the keys: optimum 6.
A timeout forward of exactly(2) requests deposits 2 into the mint's input queue: optimum 8.
An exactly(3) fork into the keys and a join refunding one token: optimum 14/3, k = 4.
The same fork from one budget token: optimum 2/3, k = 0.
An exactly(3) fork whose join ends in done: optimum 14/3, k = 4.
An exactly(2) fork from one budget token: optimum 1, though no mint can fire. The program is a relaxation.
A mint whose XOR branches write either key: optimum 2.
No budget token ([NU-053] AC6): optimum 0, the exact zero-slot plan.
A join refunding one token to each of two budgets: the colours multiply, infeasible.
A carrier no join re-collects ([NU-053] AC5): infeasible.
The scatter-gather net of the parity goldens: optimum 4 (the semiflow bound was 10).
A kept row with an entry outside the cone, a duplicate restricted row, a consume-only row and an unrelated cycle.
Nothing produces into the coloured place: no kept row, optimum 0.

A chain p7 -> p6 -> ... -> p0 whose every step deposits 1000 tokens for 1 (p0 coloured, 3 tokens on p7). The tableau's right-hand sides grow by a factor of 1000 a pivot, so one passes 2^63 - 1 and the solve stops at the coefficient limit.

A chain of 320 places q319 -> ... -> q000 (q000 coloured, 3 tokens on q319). Bland's rule makes one degenerate pivot a step, each updating rows that fill in triangularly, so the work passes the limit of 4000000 entry updates before the optimum 3.

A seeded composed workflow of 255 places and 341 rows (generator seed 7): a front workflow feeding a three-key mint gated by a budget of 2, a back workflow feeding the join that refunds it, and side workflows. Optimum 6.
